sources.text: The steps of the example acid casein line, up to where the whey is spun off the curd; the patent also mentions the wash water going out with the serum.

acidCasein.text: Casein carries a negative charge in milk (pH 6.6). At pH 4.6 the charge is gone, the micelles collapse and clump into curd, which is washed free of lactose and minerals, then dried and ground. Lactic acid from a starter can do the same job, but industrial acid casein is mostly made with mineral acid.
